utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Same here, Your Honour. No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 1294B and 1294A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, do you see the transcript of 1305? Isn't it an intercept which you transcribed yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-148
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: The first sentence of this intercept is the representation of a certain Colonel Cerovic. Colonel Cerovic introduces himself. True?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-148
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it true that the second person is not heard during the whole conversation, the whole intercept?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-148
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And Colonel Cerovic does not mention the name of the other person; isn't it true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-148
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: It's a very short conversation, I would be very grateful if you could read it quickly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-148
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it true that you didn't find anything in this conversation giving the name of General Krstic? You didn't find the name of General Krstic in this intercept?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-148
utterances.text: I can't remember now. It was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not asking you to remember. In the intercept you can see in front of you, you can't read the name of General Krstic, can you? Isn't it true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-148
utterances.text: The way it is written here, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: How were you able to establish that the person in question with whom Colonel Cerovic is talking to was General Krstic, since this name has not been pronounced in this intercept and since, anyway, you cannot hear the other person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-148
utterances.text: I'm telling you I can't be sure now, and I can't remember anything that would indicate that, that would serve as an indication.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it possible therefore that the second person in this intercept could not be General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-148
utterances.text: I don't know with certainty.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no other question to ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Fauveau. Mr. Josse or Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: No, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Mr. Haynes or Mr. Sarapa.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: No. I thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Soljan, do you have a re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Just a quick redirect, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it true that your practise was only to transcribe what you heard?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, in direct you are in the same position as you are in examination-in-chief. So practice has been ones there is an objection, if it is indeed a direct question, we don't allow it. So you will rephrase your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Apologies, Your Honour, I will do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's okay. I mean you ...

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Could you briefly describe the practice of how you transcribed intercepts for us, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Judge, I object. That is beyond the scope of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It is perfectly okay. It follows from -- from the general train of questions we've had on the few cross-examinations. Go ahead. Or rather, Witness, please do answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you repeat it, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Of course, sir. Could you briefly describe for us the practice of how you transcribed intercepts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-148
utterances.text: Listening to conversations, I recorded them on tape and then transcribed in a copy book.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Did you write -- so if you heard a name, did you write it down?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-148
utterances.text: Yes, yes. We immediately wrote down names and the more important events involved so as to be able to remember them better later.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir; no more questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: No more questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Soljan. We don't have questions for you, which means that your testimony ends here. On behalf of the Tribunal, I wish to thank you for having come over to give evidence. You will receive assistance to facilitate your return back home at the earliest. And we wish you all a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, may I draw your attention, please, counsel, to a confidential Prosecution motion filed on -- filed recently for leave to amend the witness list by adding one more intercept operator at -- as 92 ter witness and for protective measures. But you get it up; I will be come back to you in a moment on this. In the meantime we have these documents related to this last witness, PW-148 to deal with. Any objections as to the admission of the proposed documents? I hear none. The witness statement will become PO2387, and it will remain under seal, the pseudonym sheet also to be kept under seal will be PO2388, and then the two intercepts one that is 65 ter numbers 1298, 1294 in their respective A and B versions will be marked for identification. The one of the 21st of July, 1294 A and B will be kept under seal, and the handwritten intercept notebook number 24 PO2369, will also be kept under seal and for the time being marked for identification purposes. And that disposes of PW-148. Now, there is this Prosecution motion which refers to a witness which, according to the very volatile schedule that has -- has been forthcoming, is scheduled to testify the day after tomorrow, on Thursday. Correct me if I am wrong, Mr. McCloskey, because I am a little hesitant, a little bit hesitant in making such affirmations as things are going.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think I'm even more hesitant, Mr. President. But yes, that person is here and the -- or is about to be here and so that schedule looks like it's -- it is happening. Those next few, there's some other issues related to scheduling I can discuss though when you're ready.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Does any one of the Defence teams wish to address the Chamber on -- on this motion? As you imagine, or as you would have gathered, there is no point in even trying to apply the usual time limits allowed by the rules for responses, et cetera, because inherently it is a matter of urgency and we need to dispose of it before the day after tomorrow. May I ask you a question, Mr. McCloskey, because I don't know more than I am going to say. You propose this person as a 92 ter witness. You would be therefore relying on what, previous testimony, statement, a witness statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, if -- what -- it would likely be a very short statement. We -- because of the problem that Mr. Meek addressed yesterday, which we understand --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's why I'm raising the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We changed our normal policy and we've actually done interviewed over the phone for these sensitive witnesses to try to get something. As you know, we are bringing these witnesses on in response to a Court order, so there was a time -- a time issue, and so we were planning on seeing them when they were here for a statement. That obviously has -- hasn't worked out because they would only be brought here a day or two before they testify, so we're trying to do telephone interviews. Whether we have been able to get this person by phone and get the process going, I don't know. We can also have a very short direct of about, you know, five questions and -- without any statement, frankly, because we all know what the answer to the questions are. But we'll try to -- we will want to give the basics to them, to see if there is no training or to see if there is any other issue that they are alerted to. But we will try to contact this person by phone - I think we already have - and try to get a statement as soon as possible. In fact, the -- based on the estimates of today, we -- we're about two to three hours off on the Defence estimates, it's been so quickly. So this is our last witness for today. Mr. Nicholls has been talking to a witness this morning, and I -- and as I imagine their estimates might have been off, I said try to get this person ready for this afternoon. The person has gone home to change and can be back in about 20 minutes and -- and the statement should be out in part or about to be out. And I -- I apologise for this. You -- as you know, we have accelerated quickly and Defence has -- their estimates -- we recognise their estimates were -- you know, lawyers trying to make time estimates are -- it is a difficult process. We recognise that they were probably conservative or whatever the opposite of that was, but -- and that brings up another issue. But I think if we can take a half an hour break, we should be able to have a witness, if people are ready to do it. Otherwise we can start with that witness in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I will very quickly consult my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, before you make your decision on the request of my learned friend regarding witness 150, I have to address you. In the brief summary of this witness's testimony, my client's name is mentioned. Therefore, I would really appreciate it if this witness could start tomorrow so that we could at least read the statement that my learned friend promises to deliver to us within the next half hour so that we can at least see what it is about in my visit to the detention unit or by telephone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which witness are we -- are we talking about now? Which one? Yeah, but I want to know who the next one is, because the last one I have in my notes was this one. So I don't have an indication of who the next one is. Have you -- yeah, if you can give me the witness number.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I can give it to you. 175, protected witness 150. His number is 173.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no, 173 is the one we finished.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, 175. 175.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we can go into private session, I can say his name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go into private session for a short while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's have a 30-minute break. You will bring over this witness and we'll start hearing his evidence, if it is necessary even dispose of the witness statement and examine him in chief viva voce then we can do that. He would have been here tomorrow in any case, so we will -- at the end of the day reserve cross-examination for Madam Nikolic until tomorrow. In the meantime we will go through the whole turn, finish examination-in-chief and as many cross-examinations as we can. You will have the opportunity to consult with your client, and then cross-examine him tomorrow. I think that's fair enough for everyone. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, just one other item. I've had a chance to briefly discuss with counsel. As you know, when we saw this acceleration, we got on the phone and we've been trying to fill the gap. One of the witnesses -- and if we could go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will have a 30-minute break as promised. Ms. Nikolic can put her mind at rest that she will cross-examine the next witness tomorrow. In the meantime Mr. McCloskey has been referring to this live crime-based witness who we could start hearing possibly tomorrow and who would possibly occupy our time for the rest of the week, as I -- as I read, Mr. McCloskey, although not necessarily so. Do you wish to make any submissions in relation to this witness? I notice Mr. Lazarevic has made it quickly --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I believe we will state our position after the break, where we have time to consult our clients and other Defences.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to draw your attention to the following fact: It's becoming a habit that for the witnesses coming after the break we still don't have the version in English and we only received the B/C/S version half an hour ago. We were not able to prepare adequately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which one? I take -- will you thresh it out with the Prosecution and then -- you know that the Trial Chamber tries to secure as much possible your rights and we will see if the problem still persists after the break, and that we will deal with it after the break. Mr. Ostojic, you were -- okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, I think we will just discuss it among ourselves and address the Court this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we will have a 30-minute break starting now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, I take it no one wishes to address the Chamber before we start with this witness. Yeah, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I was hoping to address the Trial Chamber regarding the issues that were raised before the break, but I don't know whether it's proper to do it while the witness is in the courtroom. I have no problem, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is why I sent Madam Usher to inquire whether you wish to make any statements. But anyway, let's start with the witness and finish him with the caveat that I mentioned earlier. Good afternoon, to you, sir. Witness, good afternoon to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And welcome to this Tribunal. I see that you already have the text of the solemn declaration that is required from you. Please read it out aloud and that you will be your undertaking with this Tribunal that you will testify the truth. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you. Please take a seat and make yourself comfortable. We have put in place -- yeah, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour, I just wanted to for the record, bring to the Trial Chamber's attention that, as happened yesterday, the OTP laid on our desk the B/C/S transcript of the witness statement which I was able to give to my client just as they were brought back in, and I therefore would reserve any cross-examination until tomorrow, with your permission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Meek. Upon the request from the Prosecution we have granted you some protective measures, namely that you will testify under a pseudonym instead of your usual name and surname, and that visual and voice distortion have been put in place for you. I trust that these have already been explained to you and that this arrangement is to your satisfaction. If you could kindly confirm that, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So the way we are going to proceed is Mr. Nicholls who you have met already will now put some questions to you and will also address you in relation to your witness statement. And then we will have some cross-examinations today, others to follow tomorrow morning. Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Just before I begin, I would of course not object if Mr. Meek or any counsel want a few minutes now to consult with their clients. The statement, as you can see, is the -- the substance of it is about one page and five lines. So if they want that time now, there is obviously no objection from me. You don't have the statement, sorry. But it is one page and a couple of lines, so if it would be better for their clients to read that in 10 minutes, then we could do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What I suggest we do is the following, because 10 minutes are precious. Mr. Beara has the -- the statement, so he can start reading it. When we have finished with your examination-in-chief, make we can start with other cross-examinations and we will see what the situation will be at that time. Mr. Meek will have an opportunity to go near -- approach Mr. Beara and confirm with him for any instructions and then we can proceed accordingly. But I don't think it's the case of having another 10-minute break. Yes, go ahead, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: First, if I could pass the witness a pseudonym sheet, which is P02390. Now, Witness, as you know, we've given you a number, so if you could read that sheet of paper silently to yourself and confirm to the Court that your name is written on that piece of paper.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If that could be shown to my colleagues. Now, sir, is it correct that you and I met for the first time this morning and that you gave us a written statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Was that statement then read back to you in your own language?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did you sign the statement after it had been read back to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you attest that the statement is true and accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And can you also attest that if you were asked the same questions now in the courtroom your answers would be the same as they were in the statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If we could go into private session, I will read a very brief summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: In the offices of the OTP this morning the witness reviewed a binder of eight intercepts. Copies of handwritten intercepts were in this binder, and he recognised seven out of the eight as being his. He recognised that the intercept at tab 3, ERN 0078-1483 through 0078-1484, as not in his handwriting, was not one of his intercepts. The witness -- and that's 65 ter number 1316, excuse me. The witness also reviewed the printouts which corresponded to the seven handwritten intercepts which he had transcribed, and he reviewed the original notebooks and also recognised his handwriting for those same seven intercepts in the notebook and confirmed that he had indeed recorded and transcribed those intercepts. That's the end of my summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you have questions for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Just -- just one, your answer -- Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Witness, was my summary correct from your recollection of your statement this morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: The statement will be PO2389 under seal when we move to tender it. Thank you, I have no further questions at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, sir. You said that you had the opportunity today, before signing your statement, to hear it back. It was read back to you in your own language; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You didn't have the opportunity to read it for yourself, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please tell me, you said amongst other things that for the first two months of your work during this facility that we mentioned - I'm not going to mention its name - you worked on jamming the communications of the army of Republika Srpska; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me other than yourself how many of your colleagues worked on the same job in that period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it possible that it was just you carrying out this work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true if I said that several of you were doing the same kind of work, but you are not able to tell us exactly how many of your colleagues?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. I can't tell you the exact number now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Two months after that you were transferred to a different post, different duties. And did your colleagues remain at the same work that they did up until you were transferred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement you said that you were not involved in any typing, encryption, and dispatch of the intercepts that you recorded, that other people did those jobs. Can you tell me how many people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember how many of you there were in that unit or section that intercepted conversations in that installation where you worked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us on what kind of equipment did you work? And I mean you personally.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: I have it all written down. I can't tell you off the cuff.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say you have it in writing, do you mean your own personal documentation, or maybe you believe it is on some official file?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: It's in -- it's an official file; I don't have it with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us roughly how long you worked with that piece of equipment you had?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: I could not give you a specific time-frame.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You had opportunity today, or maybe one of the previous days, to review the copy books shown you by the Prosecution. Can you tell me whether those copy books, that you kept yourself all alone, or they were used jointly by different operators?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: It's not the case that everybody had their own copy book, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me how many operators used one and the same copy book?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: No, I couldn't tell you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just for the record, where we see "copy book," it's notebook, so that we couldn't confuse the two as if they were the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me if these are the copy books or notebooks shown you by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, were they official notebooks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you receive those notebooks from the command of your unit or did you buy them yourselves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: We got them from the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Was it obvious that the notebook was received from the command? Was it distinguishable as such?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: Well, they were brought to us, to that location.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say they were brought to you, can you tell me by whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: Well, the people who were in charge of those things, whose job it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Those were not the same people who worked with you on the same shift?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember if more than one notebook was filled during a particular time period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: While you were working on your shift and while you were listening to and recording intercepts, was there only one notebook going around or were several of them kept at the same time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: There were several of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you duty-bound to enter dates into the notebooks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you record the date every time when entering a conversation as recorded on the tape?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say, "I believe so," I believe it was entered, do you mean to say that possibly someone else would enter the date if you failed to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: I don't remember now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You said in your statement that you remained at that location doing that job until September or October 1995. Can you tell me if you have that written down in your military service book? I mean the date, the exact date when you left that facility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is there any date entered in your military service book for your final departure from the service?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Was it after September 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Zivanovic. Ms. Nikolic or Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think, Your Honour, that in view of certain changes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You will reserve it?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- there exists, compared to the summary, I think we could provide that before the end of the day, yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right, okay. Let's move on to the Borovcanin Defence. In the meantime, Mr. Meek, I suggest, having heard now Ms. Nikolic, that you try to approach your client to see whether he has any instructions to give. When I say you, it's Mr. Ostojic or your colleague who speaks the language. Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, I'd like to ask you only a couple of questions regarding your method of work. Did it occur that you identified participants in a conversation without their identifying themselves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: Sometimes I could identify them by voice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic, we have absolutely no problem with Mr. Beara leaving the courtroom to give instructions to your colleagues. At the same time, we need his consent to proceed in his absence. All right. I take it that reading -- reading through your lips in Serbo-Croat, that you have given your consent.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BEARA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, sorry for the interruption, Mr. Stojanovic. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us, if you did not identify the speakers by voice how else could you identify them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: Well, according to the style of speech. I'm talking about cases when we didn't hear their names said, spoken.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that you personally were able to identify some of the participants by their style of speech?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: Well, if those speakers had had numerous conversations, then yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you would identify such a speaker, would you note down, among other things, that you had identified the speaker by voice or his characteristics of speech?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: If we were not sure we would write a sign to make that obvious.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me what sign you used to denote that you were not certain about the identity of the speakers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: Maybe a question mark or maybe just the initial.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you write in the transcripts only the things that you could hear clearly or also the things that you thought you heard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: For the most part we wrote down what we heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "for the most part," does that imply there were situations when you wrote down things you thought you'd heard or you assumed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: We would write down things like "audibility poor," "interference," "cannot make out," et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did it ever happen that you wrote down the name of a speaker without being certain of his identity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we now see in e-court please Prosecution Exhibit P01352D, sorry. And for those of us who follow it here it's tab 5, an intercept that we received from the OTP attached to the set of documents for this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 0320-4832. Sorry, PO1341, 01341.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just wanted to assure the witness - I hadn't done so before court - this is not being broadcast, that these documents, people outside the courtroom cannot see, just to put his mind at rest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you for pointing that out, Mr. Nicholls. And the witness can put his mind at rest that it isn't. Is that the page you had in mind, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. If we could just move a page up, because we need to see the heading or the letterhead.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: The previous page.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the previous page. Thank you. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at it? Do you see this passage where they mention azimuth frequency, the hour is 11:25, the participants -- can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let us read it together. When it says "participants," we see "Rajko -- Colonel Cerovic," and in brackets "assumed" or "assumption." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me what could that mean, that the participant in that conversation was Colonel Cerovic, in brackets "assumption" or "assumed"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: The conversation was difficult to hear and it had been already recorded, so it is written that it -- we assume it was Colonel Cerovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would this change your previous answer when you said that you never wrote down the names of participants unless you were sure?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sorry to object, but that is not a fair characterisation. The previous answer was if he wasn't sure it would be noted in some fashion, not that he never wrote down a name if -- as it was put to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are correct, but I think the witness can answer the question. The answer very simply -- the question very simply put, if I could phrase it a little differently is, looking at this intercept here or this transcript why did you put down the name of Cerovic in this case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since I was not alone, there were other colleagues together with me and we all listened to those conversations together, maybe one of the colleagues came to listen to the conversation together with us and maybe he told us that he was -- this was the man. It could be that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to take the witness again to one of his previous answers. On page 79, lines 6, 7 and 8, to my question, "Did it ever occur that you wrote down the name of a participant in a conversation without being sure of his identity?", you answered, "No." My question to you now, after this explanation you gave, would be as follows: Did it ever occur that you wrote down the name of a participant in a conversation without being sure of his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: I've told you already that several colleagues listened and re-listened to these intercepts and we had more than one conversation involving a particular person, so based on that we probably concluded it was Colonel Cerovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So you are telling us today that you are not certain?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, he is not saying that. I don't think he's ever said that. Let me take over for a short while. Witness, you have in the line below where we have the azimuth and the frequency, Pukovnik Cerovic, and then in brackets, "[pretpostavka]." Based on what you have testified earlier, namely that if you were not sure you wouldn't put down the name of the interlocutor, what are we to conclude seeing those names or those -- those words in this particular transcript of -- of the intercept? What should the Trial Chamber and everyone else who is listening conclude from that? That you were sure or that you were not sure?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was not sure, but I just told you my colleagues listened to it as well, and we arrived at that conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That answers your question very clearly, Mr. Stojanovic, and we can move to the next, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for this assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: To conclude let us see in e-court PO1341B. That is the intercept concerned in B/H/S [as interpreted]. Sir, do you see this intercept?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is that your handwriting, did you write that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that it is written there in your hand, U-c-x, and above that "Rajko," and then in brackets "[re: module]." And after that "p-u-k," meaning Colonel, Cerovic. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: After the word Colonel Cerovic, you did not write supposedly, or assumed, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: Well, it says here "according to modulation."

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Then I would ask you this: Behind the words Colonel Cerovic is the word "assumption" written in your hand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: No, not here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that when you were listening to that conversation and transcribing it you were certain that one of the speakers was Colonel Cerovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: I have already answered that question. According to voice modulation we assumed it was Colonel Cerovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you needn't labour any further on this because it has been cleared by the witness. This was a team effort. As far as he is concerned, he wasn't sure, but others were. And the conclusion that it was Cerovic was because of the modulation which meant something to some -- to one member of the team at least. So I don't think we need to labour it any further.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if this is clear, then we have no further questions. And we conclude here. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Notebook 104, is it indeed -- could the witness be shown P2244, 2244. Could you please show page 1895, the four last digits. And in e-court it's page 24. Sir, have you written as the date 16 July 95, did you write that date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you now go to page finishing with two digits, 97? Could you show the top of the page? That's page 26. This is indeed the end of the intercept which started under 16 July 1995, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And you see the intercept which starts just under that, frequency is indicated, the channel?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment. What's the problem, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: There is no problem, I just sensed that the witness had a problem with the screen and the pages, but the book is right next to him, I just wanted him to know he can look at the book, if he needs to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, look at the book and look at the last two or three pages that you looked at previously and just confirm again that those three pages are indeed a transcript of the intercept which -- although you didn't date it yourself, is dated 16th of July, 1995. That there are no other transcripts in between, in other words. Look at the notebook itself.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And what was the question to me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The question was the following: A couple of minutes ago Madam Fauveau referred you to two pages before where you were asked whether you had put down the date 16.7.95 yourself, and you said no. Now, starting from that page until you come -- until you come to the page which ends at the top with the last four digits 1897. "Are we still dealing with the same transcript, with the same intercept of 16.7.95, or is there any other transcript that intervened in the meantime?"

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not sure whether the date refers to the top or the bottom part of the page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: To the top part of the page. Madam Usher, can you help him, please? Start with the page where you have 16.07.95 written, handwritten there. And then take him to page 1897, to the first part of that page before we have another intercept. In those pages that you have seen, do we only have that intercept of 16.07.95, or do we also have other intercepts before we come to the next one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have this intercept of 1948 hours; that's my intercept. The rest are not mine. I didn't take them -- tape them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I leave him in your hands, Ms. Fauveau, and I suggest that you go straight to the next intercept and ask him why it's 109 and what happened in the meantime, because I suppose that's where you were heading.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, Witness, in the next intercept, the frequency is indicated as well as the channel, and numbers 1.09, which would certainly be the 1st September. Could you please explain how after 16 July there is an intercept of the 1st of September?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: I couldn't answer that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I have no other question to ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Nothing, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes, one or two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Witness, in July of 1995 would you have said that relative to your colleagues you were an inexperienced intercept operator?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: Well, no, you couldn't say that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: One question in private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Was it a regular event for you to consult colleagues as to the voices you were hearing to help with identification?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: Just in case something couldn't be heard well or if there was some interference or something.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Moving on from that, were you given orders as to what frequencies you should listen to on any particular day or in any particular period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: There was that too.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And a slightly different question. Were you given orders as to what particular subjects you should be listening out for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: There were no specific or explicit subjects, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And lastly, one technical question. Was the equipment you had capable of monitoring a frequency of 144 megahertz or thereabouts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: I don't remember that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'm not surprised, but anyway. Can we move on then to a couple of specific intercepts. As you've already told us, in some conversations that you listened to it wasn't necessary for you to have to recognise the voices because the people who were speaking told you who they were. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: It's a long time ago now, but can you help me as to this: Around about the 26th of July were you interested in the movement of VRS troops in the Zepa area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: I really couldn't answer that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I'm going to have you shown a document to see if it helps you remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Could P1353B be put on e-court, and for those of us who have it in hard copy, that's behind tab 7 in our binders. We will need to go down to the bottom of that page, and in due course we'll have to go over the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Witness, can you see the -- the date there, the 26th of July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Would you read that page down to the bottom of the page and then go over the page, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: Just at the bottom of the page?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: No, I want you to read the bottom of the page and then the next page.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: There is the frequency, 255.950, then 8.07, AR3000, participants, Major Jevdevic and Vinko.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: That's my fault. I didn't mean for you to read it out loud, just read it to remind yourself what you wrote. So read it to the bottom of the page and then over the following page, would you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: To read it to myself silently?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes, please. And then I'll ask you some questions. Feel free to tell me when you've finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Haynes, does he have to read the whole page?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: No, not really. I will put the questions to him and if he needs to look at anything further, he can do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, this is one of those occasions, isn't it, where the -- the identity of the speakers comes from what they said during the course of the conversation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: Yes, we saw already at the beginning who the people were.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And can I take it these were not voices that you recognised?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: They introduced themselves here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, I -- it really isn't important, but if they hadn't introduced themselves, I am suggesting to you that you wouldn't have known who they were from their voices.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-150
utterances.text: Probably when I -- if I heard them several times over I would be able to recognise them by their voices.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to move on. It's not important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Microphone not activated] Either today or tomorrow, because I wouldn't like it stay longer than the scheduled time, because of the other Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I've got three or four more questions. I can conclude them tomorrow, if you wish. This witness has to come back anyway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think it's better because we overstayed yesterday and I wouldn't like to do it again today. So we stand adjourned until tomorrow. Witness, it is important between now and tomorrow you do not talk to anyone on the subject matter that you are testifying about. Stay away with other -- from other witnesses or members of the Prosecution or anyone else for that matter. I thank you. Good afternoon to everyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 24th day of January, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.45 p.m.,
